@ahg-g @hex108 I'm thinking whether we really need to implement a kubelet provider. To me, what kubelet wants is just to call some functions in scheduler, is it really mandatory for them to comply with scheduler framework? If no, I would suggest just moving all the code in `predicates.go` to kubelet, which should be the safest way. I'm going to create a test PR (#87342) verifying it.

Exactly. kubelet run general predicates as admission. Moving them to kubelet is the right approach.

issue_context.title: Define a scheduler algorithm provider for kubelet
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

Define algorithm providers in terms of plugins instead of predicates for kubelet.

Ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86162

**Why is this needed**:

Predicates will be deprecated.

/sig scheduling
/assign
comments: /retitle Define a scheduler algorithm provider for kubelet

According to my actual experience, in addition to the default provider for kubelet, a custom algorithm is also necessary. 

The scenario is: the user needs to shield some of the factors that trigger the eviction of the kubelet, thereby reducing the risk of the application.

I have done most of the work for this issue. Howerver there is a problem I have not solved.

When [`predicates.GeneralPredicates`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go#L92) fails because of insufficient resources, kubelet will try to recover from it.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/36e40fb850293076b415ae3d376f5f81dc897105/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go#L103

It will retry to evict pods to saitisfy the insufficient amount.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/36e40fb850293076b415ae3d376f5f81dc897105/pkg/kubelet/preemption/preemption.go#L68-L86

Howerver, there is no such information in `framework.Status`: when we convert predicate messages, we do not put `InsufficientAmount` to the reasons, because we could not aggregate them if reasons are like `Insufficient CPU 200`, `Insufficient CPU 300` and `Insufficient CPU 400`.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/36e40fb850293076b415ae3d376f5f81dc897105/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1/interface.go#L100-L103

How about adding an field `extraInfo` in `Status` to contain these similar messages?  Then we could parse `InsufficientAmount` from them. Any suggestion for it? @ahg-g

review_comments: Are we going to use the `name` (prefilter or filter) somewhere? If not, we can simplify this data structure (map) by just using the status.

As said in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86803#issuecomment-573513174, add `extranInfos` to provide extra info for Status. Howerver it is only needed for kubelet now.  Any comment/suggestion for it? 

cc @ahg-g @Huang-Wei

I can't think of a good way without modifying the struct either. Another option is to make reasons as `[]interface{}`, so that we can adapt to the simple case (string) as well as complex case (InsufficientResource reason).
I suppose this will break some tests? As in the before, it can be something like "OutOfMemroy", but it's not right now.
